assertions.source: the empty dressing is reading-3-feasible (4/8 proton, 4/8 neutron), so the cost-minimal word is the 9-letter core+quark with NO gluon dressing. The live model is k = 2

Applying the same exclusion to the dressing gives k = 1 (length 10), NOT k = 2. So the live budget is unselected under both conventions

assertions.name: the_cost_minimal_set_does_NOT_pin_a_unique_trace
assertions.source: proton 4 words / 2 traces, neutron 4 / 2. FrobeniusSelected.cost_eq gives equal COST, not a unique word, and measured the words do not agree on the trace. A 2-fold degeneracy survives the selection and is NOT closed here

description: Reading 3 admits every dressing count, so it does not fix the crossing budget. The corpus's own selection principle does: FrobeniusSelected takes the MINIMAL-COST reading-3-feasible candidate with cost = crossing count (the Lean's own instantiation, which selects beta_Bor for the core). Applied to the dressing that gives k = 0 -- the 9-letter word, no gluon crossings -- and k = 1 if the empty dressing is excluded the way frobeniusSelected_nil forced for the core. Either way the live 11-letter nuc11_interleaved (k = 2) is NOT what the principle selects. The principle fixes the BUDGET, not the word: four assignments tie at k = 0 carrying two distinct traces per nucleon. And reading 1 is feasible NOWHERE in this family (0 of 8/48/288/1728), including at the EVEN lengths the parity theorem permits -- so it is annihilating outright, not by parity, correcting my own framing.

cost_function.caveat: extending the H_3 core's cost to the dressing is an extrapolation of the corpus's principle, not a theorem
